- When sentiment is strongly bullish (≥0.7) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next period.
- When sentiment is bearish (≤0.3) and prices are trending down, model often underestimates; adjust upward by 1–2% to avoid missing sharp reversals.
- After a price spike (forecast > true outcome by >5%), model frequently overcorrects in the following period; dampen forecast by 2–5% for 2–3 periods.
- If sentiment shifts from bullish to bearish mid-horizon, model often fails to adjust; check for mean reversion in 3–5 period window and reduce forecast slope.
- For 30-day forecasts, model consistently underestimates true outcomes when sentiment is volatile (±0.3–0.7) — apply a +1.5% bias correction for volatile sentiment periods.
- If recent history shows strong mean reversion (e.g., 3–5 consecutive days of price decline), model tends to ignore it; increase forecast sensitivity to recent low prices by 1–2%.
- When sentiment is neutral (0.3–0.7) and price is near 30-day moving average, model often overfits to recent highs; cap forecast at 1.5–2% above recent low.
